_comment: The cases are SYNTHETIC memory stores, not copies of a real one: this
repository is public and a real auto-memory store holds an operator's
private working notes. Each case is the same four-memory store - one memory
carrying the strict `**Superseded YYYY-MM-DD.**` marker, one dependent that
links to it, one newer dependent, and one unrelated memory that uses the
word 'superseded' in PROSE - and only the first dependent's `modified` date
differs between cases. So the verdict can only come from comparing that
date against the marker, which is what the anchor removes.
No git and no binary beyond python3: the cases are plain files, so this

cases.name: bad-stale-dependent
cases.why: rollout-order.md (modified 2026-02-01) links [[widget-placement]], superseded 2026-03-10. The issue's observed instance: the supersession was recorded in one node and never reached the node that links to it. If this scores GOOD the checker cannot see the propagation gap at all.

cases.name: good-current
cases.why: The same store with rollout-order.md modified 2026-03-15, after the supersession. A checker that flags every link to a superseded memory, regardless of date, fails here - and the unrelated memory's prose 'superseded' must not count as a marker.

cases.name: unknown-undated
cases.anchor_expect_reason: The anchor recognises no memory as superseded, so it never reaches the comparison that discovers an undated dependent; it can only answer clean. Deriving the undecidable population requires the marker detection whose removal is the anchor's whole blindness.
cases.why: rollout-order.md has no modified date. Whether it predates the supersession cannot be known, and that must read unknown (exit 3), never clean - 15 of 48 memories in the store that motivated #1440 carry no date.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED because the gate is new: the honest 'before' is no checker at all, which cannot be run. This variant is the gate with supersession-marker detection replaced by `return None`, so no memory is ever superseded and all three of this control's cases read clean (not every input: an unclosed frontmatter still reads unknown and a missing root unreadable, because those paths are untouched). It MISSES the known-bad case and AGREES with the gate on the known-good one, which proves the marker detection is what produces the verdict.
